title: Actionable written feedback on workplace-based assessments in an internal medicine residency
subtitle: Quality improvement with PDSA cycles and a weekly run chart, October 2026 to March 2027
statement: Only about one in four written comments on the residency's workplace-based assessment forms names a specific behaviour, a gap and a next step, so residents learn little from them and the competence committee cannot rely on them. The project will test a change package in PDSA cycles to raise the weekly proportion of actionable comments, tracked on a run chart with balancing measures for form completion and timeliness and a check by resident gender.
whoAffected: Ninety internal medicine residents, the faculty who assess them, the competence committee that makes progress decisions, and indirectly the patients whose care depends on residents' skills improving.
whatHurts: Generic praise gives residents nothing to act on, weak comments make progress decisions harder to defend, and feedback of different quality for women and men residents would be unfair.
currentPractice: One free-text box per form, no guidance on what a useful comment contains, and no monitoring of comment quality.
whyNow: The committee's review of 200 forms showed the problem, faculty meeting time has been approved, and the administrator can relabel the field now and add a second one in January.
constraints: No funding. Rating is done by the two chief residents in two hours of protected time a week. The software administrator can relabel the existing feedback field now but cannot add a second field before January 2027. Faculty meetings are monthly and can give 20 minutes to the project.
patientCenteredGoal: Residents receive specific, usable feedback that helps them become safer physicians, whatever their gender.
summary: Problem framed as a program-level QI project to raise actionable written feedback on workplace-based assessments.
